strengths.item: The paper is well organized in a standard ICLR format, with clear section numbering, consistent margins, readable body text, and a logical progression from empirical findings to the Adaptive RR method.

The writing is generally understandable, and the paper’s main claims are easy to locate: data augmentation, critic plasticity, early-stage intervention, and the replay-ratio method are presented in a coherent sequence.
Captions are generally informative and specific, often explaining both the visual setup and the intended takeaway, which helps reviewers connect figures to the surrounding argument.
The boxed “Adaptive Replay Ratio” callout and displayed equation are visually clear and help make the method and measurement definitions easy to inspect.

weaknesses.item: Many figures contain multiple small subplots, tiny legends, small axis/tick labels, and dense shaded confidence bands, making detailed inspection difficult without zooming.
Several pages are visually crowded around figures, especially pages with multiple training-curve plots and text wrapping tightly around visuals.
Some plots rely heavily on color and light confidence shading, which may reduce readability in grayscale or for accessibility.

dimension_review.evidence_summary: The PDF inspection found a polished, standard ICLR-style layout with readable text, clear headings, and informative captions. Page-level observations noted that Figures 1–10 are generally clean and relevant, but many are compressed: Figure 1 has small legends and labels, Figure 2 is squeezed into the right-column area, Figures 3–6 have small subplot labels or visually dense legends/shading, Figure 8 is relatively small beside text, and Figures 9–10 require zooming for detailed inspection. The boxed Adaptive Replay Ratio callout on page 8 and Equation 1 on page 5 were visually clear.
dimension_review.rationale: The paper is clearly written and well structured overall, and reviewers should be able to follow the argument and verify the main evidence. However, the presentation is not excellent because many figures are visually compressed and somewhat difficult to inspect at page scale. These are noticeable but not severe issues, so the appropriate score is good rather than excellent.
